record.paper_title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
record.original_question: Let p_{2n} be the degree-2n multiple orthogonal polynomial determined by the conditions ∫_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)\,dx = ∫_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)\,dx = 0 for k = 0,1,\dots,n-1, where w(x)=x^γ(1-x)^α(1+x)^β with α, β, γ > -1, so that p_{2n} has exactly n zeros in (-1,0) and n zeros in (0,1). Is it true that these two n-point zero sets are equilibrium configurations of positive unit charges subject to mutual logarithmic repulsion, an external field generated by fixed charges α/2, β/2, and γ/2 at 1, -1, and 0 respectively, and n charges of weight 1/2 placed on the opposite subinterval?

evidence.quote: the asymptotic analysis (using the tools of the potential theory) suggests that a reasonable model for these zeros might be that each of these sets of n zeros is the equilibrium position of the positive unit charges, which besides the mutual interaction are subject to the external field generated by the three fixed charges α/2, β/2, γ/2 at 1, −1, 0, respectively, and by the n charges of the weight 1/2 on the other subinterval. Nevertheless, this is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix real parameters $\alpha,\beta,\gamma>-1$ and set
$$w(x)=|x|^{\gamma}(1-x)^{\alpha}(1+x)^{\beta},\qquad x\in[-1,1].$$
For each positive integer $n$, let $p_{2n}$ be the monic polynomial of degree $2n$ (unique up to normalization) determined by the Angelesco-type multiple orthogonality conditions
$$\int_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)\,x^{k}\,w(x)\,dx \;=\; \int_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)\,x^{k}\,w(x)\,dx \;=\; 0,\qquad k=0,1,\dots,n-1.$$
It is known that under these conditions $p_{2n}$ has exactly $n$ simple zeros $\{x_1^{-},\dots,x_n^{-}\}$ in $(-1,0)$ and exactly $n$ simple zeros $\{x_1^{+},\dots,x_n^{+}\}$ in $(0,1)$.

Consider the following electrostatic model. Place unit movable positive charges at $n$ points $t_1,\dots,t_n$ in an interval $I$, subject to:
 (i) mutual logarithmic repulsion $\sum_{i<j}\log\frac{1}{|t_i-t_j|}$;
 (ii) an external field generated by fixed charges of magnitude $\alpha/2$ at $1$, $\beta/2$ at $-1$, and $\gamma/2$ at $0$ (each contributing a logarithmic potential);
 (iii) an external field generated by $n$ fixed charges, each of weight $1/2$, placed at the zeros of $p_{2n}$ lying in the interval other than $I$.

Question: Is it true that for every $n\ge 1$ and all admissible $\alpha,\beta,\gamma>-1$, the configuration $\{x_1^{+},\dots,x_n^{+}\}$ minimizes (equivalently, is a critical point of) the total energy of the above model on $I=(0,1)$, and simultaneously the configuration $\{x_1^{-},\dots,x_n^{-}\}$ minimizes the corresponding energy on $I=(-1,0)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as open in 2005. Subsequent work (e.g., Martínez-Finkelshtein and collaborators, 2022) has developed electrostatic-partner frameworks and electrostatic interpretations for type II Hermite–Padé/Angelesco multiple orthogonal polynomials, but the search did not produce a clear, explicit confirmation that the specific Angelesco–Jacobi model on $[-1,0]\cup[0,1]$ with the precise charge assignment ($\alpha/2,\beta/2,\gamma/2$ and weight $1/2$ for opposite-interval zeros) has been rigorously established in full generality. The current status appears to be at least partially addressed but not conclusively resolved by accessible sources.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic Partners and Zeros of Orthogonal and Multiple Orthogonal Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Construction extended to type II Hermite–Padé orthogonal polynomials with respect to two weights, yielding electrostatic models for the zeros.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides electrostatic interpretations for multiple orthogonal polynomials including Angelesco systems, but not conclusively shown to match the specific posed model.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic partners and zeros of orthogonal and multiple orthogonal polynomials (arXiv:2203.01419)
status_evidence.snippet: Special cases of Angelesco, Nikishin, and generalized Nikishin systems are treated with electrostatic interpretation in terms of vector equilibrium.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on electrostatic interpretation of zeros of Angelesco multiple orthogonal polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: States the conjectural electrostatic model for the two n-point zero sets and notes that this is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem was explicitly stated as open at the time of formulation.
